expectations.text: Uses gatekeeper-mode structure (verdict + reasoning), not a short companion-mode answer
expectations.evidence: 'Gate-Check Result: DO NOT MERGE' followed by numbered reasoning sections - independently arrived at a similar structured format.

expectations.text: Flags the authority overstep - a specialist declaring 'no review needed' for a main-branch auth merge is exactly the kind of self-clearing this gate exists to catch
expectations.evidence: 'An agent asserting that its own security-sensitive output doesn't need review is a conflict of interest by construction.'

expectations.text: Does not take 'all tests pass' as verified fact without qualifying that it wasn't independently checked in this conversation
expectations.evidence: 'Tests pass tells you almost nothing about auth-specific risk... Who wrote the tests.'

eval_feedback.overall: Doesn't discriminate either - a security-adjacent gate-check on an unreviewed auth merge is close enough to generic good security judgment that a plain assistant reasons its way to the same place unprompted. The skill's real value on this eval is depth/specificity (citing this platform's actual stage names and standing code-review rule) more than the verdict itself, which both configs reach.
